display_long_description:
With VRtravelX, you experience a sunny Friday morning at Frankfurt’s Römer as the city slowly comes to life. Directly across the square stands the Römer, Frankfurt’s famous city hall, where weddings take place on Fridays. Early in the morning, the square begins to change: cleaning crews prepare the historic setting, the first people cross the cobblestones, and little by little the heart of the old city fills with life. Between the half-timbered houses, the Fountain of Justice, and St. Nicholas Church, a calm and authentic urban scene begins to unfold.

VRtravelX makes this place not only visible, but also audible and deeply atmospheric. Bells begin to ring from St. Nicholas Church on the right side of the square, from other churches in the city center, and from the area around nearby St. Paul’s Church. St. Paul’s Church is one of the key places in German democratic history, because in 1848 the first freely elected all-German National Assembly met there and worked on a constitution. 

Behind the row of historic half-timbered buildings, you can also hear Frankfurt Cathedral, the great church closely connected to the imperial elections and coronation traditions of the Holy Roman Empire.
With VRtravelX, this morning becomes a vivid moment of time and place. Tourists gradually enter the square, take photos and selfies, and look toward the Römer, the fountain, and the historic facades.
